If the glass left a cut in the tire itself, place a tire boot (or even a folded energy bar wrapper or a bit of strong tape) between the tube and tire to prevent the tube from bulging out.

**5. Ride Gently:**  
If you’re able to reinflate and keep going, take it easy—avoid sharp turns, bumps, and hard braking, especially on slick paths. Lower pressure can mean less grip and more risk of rim damage.

If the leak gets worse or you run out of air, it’s better to stop and do a full tube change or patch job—even if it takes time—than risk damaging your rim or having a blowout.
